interpretation: At both K33 and K35, A detects10/16 and B13/16. Equalizing review counts locally therefore does not eliminate the three-detection B advantage observed at locked cutoffs. The unequal locked review volumes A35/B33 alone do not explain that advantage.

Within the same equal-review ranking policy, increasing K35toK50 adds4 low-quality detections to A and0toB; A then detects14/16 versus B13/16. This is evidence of budget-dependent ranking-curve crossing within the observed cohort, not a rule that changing policies must reverse performance.

The comparison of original locked A35/B33 with top50 per method changes both the decision constraint and actual review volume. The added same-K display separates those quantities descriptively; it does not estimate a causal policy effect.

Each external low-quality patient changes detection by6.25percentage points. The K50 A advantage is one patient, so these counts do not establish population superiority. Original H1-H3 and original top50 intervals and plan identity remain unchanged.

The new three-budget display is post hoc and descriptive. K33/35 are post hoc matched counts from archived transferred-cutoff review volumes. K50 is the original protocol supplementary budget, repeated here without reclassification. No budget was selected to maximize significance, and no p-values, new intervals or bootstrap estimates were calculated.
